newsitem.title: USA: Ind. Gov okays arena and convention center bills.
newsitem.headline: Ind. Gov okays arena and convention center bills.

text.p: Indiana Gov. Frank O'Bannon on Wednesday approved bills for partial bond financing of a new Indiana Pacers basketball arena and expansion of the Indianapolis Convention Center and RCA Dome complex.
O'Bannon approved a new professional sports development district in downtown Indianapolis to capture sales and income taxes to back $50 million of bonds for a new $175 million arena.

The governor also signed a bill enabling increases in the hotel/motel tax, rental car tax and a broader application of an existing ticket tax for partial funding of the convention center and dome expansion.
Lawmakers had approved those measures last week in breaking an impasse over workers' compensation benefits that had stalled consideration of the plans.

O'Bannon's approval for the convention center comes one day after Indianapolis Mayor Stephen Goldsmith announced a $30 million grant from the Lilly Endowment for the $45 million convention center project.

Goldsmith called the grant offer a critical non-tax funding component for the convention center and dome expansion that "allows us the freedom to use projected revenues from the proposed increase in the auto rental tax on possible dome improvements, or other needs."
The City Council is expected to vote on the plans at a meeting on Monday, Goldsmith said. The hotel/motel tax has been designated wholly to the convention center and dome project, he noted.
